correctness.rationale: For size-n multiplicity vectors x,y, correcting up to n-3 deletions is equivalent to no common 3-submultiset, i.e. I(x,y)=sum_i min(x_i,y_i)<=2. Distinct words with any multiplicity >=3 (heavy) cannot be assigned the same heavy coordinate, so at most q heavy codewords. For any two vectors with all entries <=2 (light), I(x,y)>=sum_i(x_i+y_i-2)=2n-2q>=4 when n>=q+2, so at most one light; for n>=2q+1 light words do not exist. The q pure vectors n*e_i meet the bound, and when q+2<=n<=2q the added light vector with n-q twos and 2q-n ones has sum n and intersects each pure vector by at most 2. For n=q+1 the explicit odd/even-q two-light witness yields >=q+2, proving the lower threshold sharp. Equality q heavy words forces exactly one singleton high-multiplicity coordinate for each alphabet symbol. This is a genuine all-parameter proof; independent exact pairwise intersection checks of constructions and lower-boundary witnesses for q=2..9 support it.
